This is important because I'm fucking tired of hiding my disease in public. I'm type 2 diabetic. I'm not fat, my doctor has, in fact, ordered me to gain weight as I'm only 4lbs over an underweight BMI. Type 2 diabetes runs in my family, because, yes it can be genetic. It's just very rare, and means something very different for me than what it does for a fat.

My body doesn't process insulin correctly. For whatever reason, my insulin receptors are fucked, and they don't respond well. Over my life, they will respond less and less well, and eventually they will just crap out and I'll be on a downward spiral of insulin dependence that will kill me. Hopefully, if my mother is a good model for my future, that will be a very long time in the future. She just went on insulin last year at 67, and her glucose is only mildly problematic.

I put in 90m at the gym every day and eat a very rigorously planned diet. I can eat out, but I have to watch carbs, and I log EVERY meal. Every one. I don't get cheat days, I don't get days off, because I don't want to die. As a result, my fasting glucose is typically 75-85, and my post-meal glucose is usually below 120. This is on the low side of normal, but only because I work at it. A lot of things tip the balance. A six hour flight and time change, for instance will push my fasting into the 90s for a day or two. Getting sick does the same thing. It takes a lot of discipline to stay normal.

Because I work at it, I'm "undiagnosable", which means I'm asymptomatic under normal conditions, but I am still diabetic. If I eat pizza, for instance, my glucose spikes more than normal. Which is why I don't eat pizza. Or pasta. Or rice. Or tortilla chips. Or any of those delicious foods that fuck with my sugars. I eat lean meats, green veggies, and a very planned level of starches and grains. My HbA1c is 5.2, which is below even prediabetes diagnosis criteria.

But here's the thing, this is a serious disease, and part of staying healthy is testing. I baseline myself before every meal to plan how many carbs I can have (If I'm low, in the 60s, for instance, I can have more fun than if I'm in the low 90s, I get about 20g extra carbs for my meal!), and I test after meals to check my highs. Getting these test results improves my control and helps me check for changes in my metabolism. Right now I'm focusing on strength training in an effort to get even more control.
